title: Guest Runway: SDKenV Rapid Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This note describes a compact, rehearsal-friendly SDKenV (sandbox environment) flow for short demo sessions and guest workshops — the "Guest Runway". The goal is to get a developer or non-engineer visitor from zero -> observable sample call within 10 minutes, with deterministic fallbacks and telemetry probes so hosts can triage quickly during live sessions.

Audience:
- Solutions engineers running 1:1 product demos
- Developer advocates running workshops or office hours
- New internal hires who need a predictable first-run experience

Design principles (must-haves):
- Ephemeral, low-friction environment provisioning (no infra tickets during demos)
- Single command to boot local proxy + sample app (cross-platform)
- Clear failure modes and immediate remediation steps for common network / auth issues
- Short rehearsal script (30–60s prompts) for hosts
- Telemetry probes (latency, token usage, error class) surfaced in a minimal dashboard widget and returned to host CLI

Quick architecture sketch:
- sdkenv-guest CLI (wrapper) that:
  1) pulls a pinned sample config from S3 (guest-runway/pinned-v1.json)
  2) requests an ephemeral guest token from the staging auth service (1 hour TTL)
  3) launches a tiny local proxy that rewrites requests to the Redwood hosted API or mocked endpoint based on the mode flag
  4) starts the sample app (node server or python script) on a random free port and prints the URL
- Optional: a public short link that opens the sample UI for the guest (uses signed URL)

Prereqs (host checklist):
- Machine: macOS/Linux/Windows WSL with node 18+ or python 3.10+
- Install: sdkenv-guest (npm i -g @redwood/sdkenv-guest) or pip install redwood-guest
- Slack channel: #guest-runway available for real-time support

One-command boot example (guest mode, hosted):
- sdkenv-guest boot --mode hosted --profile demo-1
What it does (happy path):
- fetch pinned config -> gives model id, endpoint URL, sample prompt set
- requests ephemeral token -> aborts if auth fails (see remediation)
- starts local proxy and sample UI -> prints URL and debug token
- starts telemetry probe pinging /health and perf endpoint -> prints simple summary

Language quick snippets (for host copy-paste)
- JavaScript (6 lines):
  import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk';
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_GUEST_KEY });
  const r = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-mini-chat-v1', input: 'Summarize product in one sentence' });
  console.log(r.text);

- Python (5 lines):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  c = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_GUEST_KEY'])
  print(c.generate('Explain in plain terms: what is Redwood Inference?'))

Common failure modes & quick remediations:
1) Ephemeral token request fails (401 / network timeout)
   - Quick check: run sdkenv-guest auth-status (prints /auth ping and reason)
   - Fixes: re-run boot, if repeated: check host's VPN firewall rules; copy-paste error: ensure macOS firewall allows outgoing connection to auth.redwood-staging.com
   - Temporary workaround: --mode mock to run against local stub (recommended for offline demos)
2) Local proxy port already in use
   - sdkenv-guest will try next free port; if UI doesn't appear, run sdkenv-guest list-ports to see conflicts. If blocked by corporate endpoint, use --no-proxy to have the sample app talk directly (less ideal for telemetry)
3) Model latency spikes ( > 3s median for 128 tokens )
   - Telemetry command: sdkenv-guest probe-latency -> prints p50/p90/p99 and last error class
   - Host action: switch to a smaller pinned model: sdkenv-guest switch-model redwood-mini-fast-v1
4) Guest sees hallucinated or unhelpful output during demo
   - Use short, deterministic prompt templates (append system: "You are a short summarizer, output <= 35 words")
   - Use --temperature 0.0 in the pinned config for predictable outputs

Telemetry & observability (minimal required probes):
- Local CLI probes: /health, /generate latency, token_count per call, error_class (4xx/5xx/connect)
- Host dashboard widget (tiny): shows last 10 calls p50/p95 plus telemetry tag (guest-id, model)
- Post-demo ingestion: sdkenv-guest upload-transport --dest=internal/guest-runs retains anonymized traces for 72h for repros

Rehearsal script (host-facing, 90s):
- 00:00–00:15: Intro the guest-runway flow: "I'll run a tiny demo environment on my laptop; you'll see a short UI and we'll test three short prompts"
- 00:15–00:40: Boot the environment: sdkenv-guest boot --mode hosted --profile demo-1 (announce URL)
- 00:40–01:00: Run prompt #1: "Summarize X" (guest watches output populate)
- 01:00–01:20: Run prompt #2: shorter constrained template, switch to temperature 0 if needed
- 01:20–01:30: If anything fails, flip to --mode mock and continue the conversation; collect telemetry with sdkenv-guest probe-latency and paste the short report into #guest-runway

Demo-ready checklist (greenlight before inviting guests):
- [ ] sdkenv-guest installed and updated to pinned release v2024-09-02
- [ ] Host machine tested with sdkenv-guest boot (no auth errors)
- [ ] Rehearsed two prompts and one fallback (mock) scenario
- [ ] Telemetry widget visible in host CLI and authenticated
- [ ] Signed short link generator tested and not expired

Developer notes / TODOs (rough):
- Move pinned config to release-candidate folder and automate pin updates via CI (todo: GH Actions job)
- Add a one-click Google Meet URL that opens the sample UI in a new tab for non-technical guests (investigate signed URL TTL)
- Add a smaller Python micro-UI for low-bandwidth guests (sketch in repo under /examples/guest-micro-ui)
- Confirm legal privacy wording for post-demo trace upload (DS-privacy review required)

Notes to self / informal fragments:
- Might want a "host-only quick reset" command that clears telemetry and returns proxy to cold state (sdkenv-guest reset-host)
- Consider embedding a short canned transcript (3 exchanges) for the mock mode so hosts can continue without network
- Slack thread: #guest-runway very useful — pin this doc there and add a short video of 60s boot
- Quick trial numbers: target <10s boot on warm laptop; <4s p50 generation for 64 tokens

Links & quick refs:
- pinned config location: s3://redwood-guest/pinned/pinned-v1.json
- repo: github.com/redwood-inference/guest-runway (WIP)
- confluence reference: DEVEXP-1742
- support slack: #guest-runway

If you're reading this as a host: please run the demo once with a colleague before the actual session. When in doubt, flip to mock mode and finish the story — guests remember the conversation, not the infra hiccups.

---
End of playbook (WIP).
